arxiv-1510-05524.title: ON THE PACKING CHROMATIC NUMBER ON HAMMING GRAPHS AND GENERAL GRAPHS
arxiv-1510-05524.description: Abstract The packing chromatic number χ ρ ​ ( G ) \chi_{\rho}(G) of a graph G G is the smallest integer k k needed to proper color the vertices of G G in such a way the distance between any two vertices having color i i be at least i + 1 i+1 .

arxiv-2206-14666.title: Conditionally Elicitable Dynamic Risk Measures for Deep Reinforcement Learning Thanks: August 8, 2026.
arxiv-2206-14666.creator: Anthony Coache, Sebastian Jaimungal, Álvaro Cartea
arxiv-2206-14666.description: Abstract We propose a novel framework to solve risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) problems where the agent optimises time-consistent dynamic spectral risk measures. Based on the notion of conditional elicitability, our methodology constructs (strictly consistent) scoring functions that are used as penalizers in the estimation procedure.

arxiv-2209-13578.title: Learning When to Advise Human Decision Makers This paper was published in Proceedings of IJCAI 2023. The data are available on the authors’ websites.
arxiv-2209-13578.creator: Gali Noti, Yiling Chen
arxiv-2209-13578.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gali Noti, Yiling Chen. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used for providing advice to facilitate human decision making in a wide range of domains, such as healthcare, criminal justice, and finance. Motivated by limitations of the current practice where algorithmic advice is provided to human users as a constant element in the decision-making pipeline, in this paper we raise the question of when should algorithms provide advice?

arxiv-2210-05720.title: Radio pulsars — two old questions (in blessed memory of Ya.N.Istomin)
arxiv-2210-05720.creator: Vasily Beskin 1,2
arxiv-2210-05720.description: Abstract We draw attention to two unanswered questions in radio pulsars’ theory. The first one concerns the inclination angles χ \chi between magnetic and rotation axes. We show that the very existence of interpulse pulsars indicates that all possible angles are realized.

arxiv-2301-04221.title: Explaining Deep Models through Forgettable Learning Dynamics
arxiv-2301-04221.creator: Ryan Benkert, Oluwaseun Joseph Aribido, Ghassan AlRegib
arxiv-2301-04221.description: Abstract Even though deep neural networks have shown tremendous success in countless applications, explaining model behaviour or predictions is an open research problem. In this paper, we address this issue by employing a simple yet effective method by analysing the learning dynamics of deep neural networks in semantic segmentation tasks.

arxiv-2302-00969.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wen-Chi Kuo, School of Mathematics. Strong convergence and convergence in probability were generalized to the setting of a Riesz space with conditional expectation operator, T T , in [ Y. Watson , Convergence in Riesz spaces with conditional expectation operators, Positivity , 19 (2015), 647-657] as T T -strong convergence and convergence in T T -conditional probability, respectively.

arxiv-2307-09761.title: Origin of Life Molecules in the Atmosphere After Big Impacts on the Early Earth
arxiv-2307-09761.creator: Nicholas F. Wogan, David C. Catling, Kevin J. Zahnle, Roxana Lupu
arxiv-2307-09761.description: Abstract The origin of life on Earth would benefit from a prebiotic atmosphere that produced nitriles, like HCN, which enable ribonucleotide synthesis. However, geochemical evidence suggests that Hadean air was relatively oxidizing with negligible photochemical production of prebiotic molecules. These paradoxes are resolved by iron-rich asteroid impacts that transiently reduced the entire atmosphere, allowing nitriles to form in subsequent photochemistry.

arxiv-2502-03377.title: Energy-Efficient UAV-assisted LoRa Gateways: A Multi-Agent Optimization Approach
arxiv-2502-03377.creator: Abdullahi Isa Ahmed, Jamal Bentahar, El Mehdi Amhoud
arxiv-2502-03377.description: Abstract As next-generation Internet of Things (NG-IoT) networks continue to grow, the number of connected devices is rapidly increasing, along with their energy demands, creating challenges for resource management and sustainability. Energy-efficient communication, particularly for power-limited IoT devices, is therefore a key research focus.

arxiv-2504-16625.title: Inducing spectral gaps for the cohomological Laplacians of Sp 2 ​ n ⁡ ( ℤ ) \operatorname{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z})
arxiv-2504-16625.creator: Piotr Mizerka, Jakub Szymański
arxiv-2504-16625.description: Abstract We show that the spectral gap of the first cohomological Laplacian Δ 1 \Delta_{1} for Sp 2 ​ n ⁡ ( ℤ ) \operatorname{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}) follows once a slightly stronger assumption holds for some Sp 2 ​ m ⁡ ( ℤ ) \operatorname{Sp}_{2m}(\mathbb{Z}) , where n ≥ m n\geq m .

arxiv-2510-16536.title: Few-Label Multimodal Modeling of SNP Variants and ECG Phenotypes Using Large Language Models for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification
arxiv-2510-16536.creator: Niranjana Arun Menon 1 , Yulong Li 3 , Iqra Farooq 2 , Sara Ahmed 2 , Muhammad Awais 2 , Imran Razzak 3
arxiv-2510-16536.description: Abstract Cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk stratification remains a major challenge due to its multifactorial nature and limited availability of high-quality labeled datasets. While genomic and electrophysiological data such as SNP variants and ECG phenotypes are increasingly accessible, effectively integrating these modalities in low-label settings is non-trivial.

arxiv-2511-04541.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: Toward World Models for Slate Recommendation Systems
arxiv-2511-04541.creator: Baptiste G. Bonin Maxime Heuillet Audrey Durand, [0.3cm] Université Laval (IID) Mila – Quebec AI Institute CIFAR AI CHAIR
arxiv-2511-04541.description: Abstract Modeling user preferences across domains remains a key challenge in slate recommendation (i.e. recommending an ordered sequence of items) research. We investigate how Large Language Models (LLM) can effectively act as world models of user preferences through pairwise reasoning over slates. We conduct an empirical study involving several LLMs on three tasks spanning different datasets.

arxiv-2512-05259.title: Age-Inclusive 3D Human Mesh Recovery for Action-Preserving Data Anonymization
arxiv-2512-05259.creator: Georgios Chatzichristodoulou, Niki Efthymiou, Panagiotis Filntisis, Georgios Pavlakos, Petros Maragos
arxiv-2512-05259.description: Abstract While three-dimensional (3D) shape and pose estimation is a highly researched area that has yielded significant advances, the resulting methods, despite performing well for the adult population, generally fail to generalize effectively to children and infants. This paper addresses this challenge by introducing AionHMR, a comprehensive framework designed to bridge this domain gap.

europmc-pmc1764438.title: Large-scale mapping and validation of Escherichia coli transcriptional regulation from a compendium of expression profiles.
europmc-pmc1764438.creator: Faith JJ, Hayete B, Thaden JT, Mogno I, Wierzbowski J, Cottarel G, Kasif S, Collins JJ, Gardner TS.
europmc-pmc1764438.description: Machine learning approaches offer the potential to systematically identify transcriptional regulatory interactions from a compendium of microarray expression profiles. However, experimental validation of the performance of these methods at the genome scale has remained elusive....

pmc-10733831.title: Improving Social Isolation and Loneliness Among Adolescents With Physical Disabilities Through Group-Based Virtual Reality Gaming: Feasibility Pre-Post Trial Study
pmc-10733831.creator: Byron Lai, Raven Young, Mary Craig, Kelli Chaviano, Erin Swanson-Kimani, Cynthia Wozow, Drew Davis, James H Rimmer
pmc-10733831.description: BackgroundAdolescents with disabilities experience alarmingly higher rates of depression and isolation than peers without disabilities. There is a need to identify interventions that can improve mental health and isolation among this underserved population. Innovations in virtual reality (VR) gaming “standalone” headsets allow greater access to immersive high-quality digital experiences, due to their relatively low cost.

pmc-10768804.title: MulinforCPI: enhancing precision of compound–protein interaction prediction through novel perspectives on multi-level information integration
pmc-10768804.creator: Ngoc-Quang Nguyen, Sejeong Park, Mogan Gim, Jaewoo Kang
pmc-10768804.description: Forecasting the interaction between compounds and proteins is crucial for discovering new drugs. However, previous sequence-based studies have not utilized three-dimensional (3D) information on compounds and proteins, such as atom coordinates and distance matrices, to predict binding affinity. Furthermore, numerous widely adopted computational techniques have relied on sequences of amino acid characters for protein representations.

pmc-11384094.title: Generation of densely labeled oligonucleotides for the detection of small genomic elements
pmc-11384094.creator: Clemens Steinek, Miguel Guirao-Ortiz, Gabriela Stumberger, Annika J. Tölke, David Hörl, Thomas Carell, Hartmann Harz, Heinrich Leonhardt
pmc-11384094.description: SummaryThe genome contains numerous regulatory elements that may undergo complex interactions and contribute to the establishment, maintenance, and change of cellular identity. Three-dimensional genome organization can be explored with fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) at the single-cell level, but the detection of small genomic loci remains challenging.

pmc-11492346.title: Modeling the significance of corporate social responsibility on green capabilities and sustainability performance
pmc-11492346.creator: Han Xiao, Abdullah Al Mamun, Mohammad Nurul Hassan Reza, Xiaofang Lin, Qing Yang
pmc-11492346.description: This study examines the complex interplay among corporate social responsibility (CSR), green dynamic capabilities, green innovation capabilities, and organizations' economic, environmental, and social performance in the current era of innovation and sustainability. The proposed framework was tested using data from 634 medium- and large-sized Chinese manufacturing firms. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was employed to analyze the data.

pmc-12110494.title: Knowledge, Attitude and Practices of Health Care Providers towards Disaster and Emergency Preparedness in Mtwara, Tanzania
pmc-12110494.creator: Silvester Walles, Emmanuel Z Chona, Menti L Ndile, Fatina B Ramadhani
pmc-12110494.description: BackgroundOver the past decade, the magnitude and intensity of reported natural and humanmade disasters have been rising globally with substantial mortality and long-term morbidity.ObjectivesTo assess the health care providers' knowledge, attitude and practices towards disaster and emergency preparedness at Ligula Regional Referral Hospital in Mtwara, Tanzania.

pmc-12467958.title: Perspectives on Alzheimer’s Disease Treatment Based on Counteracting Oxidative Stress
pmc-12467958.creator: Rafał Bilski, Stanisław Dąbkowski, Igor Kozieł, Michał Kozicki, Anna Małachowska, Mikołaj Przygocki, Oliwia Tyska, Fabio Di Domenico
pmc-12467958.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and one of the most pressing global health challenges. Increasing evidence highlights oxidative stress as a key factor in its pathogenesis, contributing to amyloid-β accumulation, tau hyperphosphorylation, neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Oxidative stress markers, detected in the bodily fluids of AD patients, are considered promising diagnostic and prognostic tools.

pmc-12563368.title: Nutrients, Food Bioactives, and Functional Foods in Gastrointestinal and Metabolic Disorders
pmc-12563368.creator: Lorena Ortega Moreno, Samuel Fernández-Tomé
pmc-12563368.description: ential ability to modulate glucose and lipid metabolism, inflammation, oxidative stress, gut microbiota composition, and gut barrier integrity [1,2,3]. The Special Topic “Nutrients, Food Bioactives, and Functional Foods in Gastrointestinal and Metabolic Disorders” has gathered 14 outstanding contributions published across different journals, including Foods, Nutrients, Antioxidants, Current Issues in Molecular Biology, and International Journal of Molecular Sciences.

pmc-13111250.title: Strategic value driven by artificial intelligence in global businesses: a bibliometric and qualitative analysis of the most influential literature
pmc-13111250.creator: Melva Jenny Zambonino-Torres, Jaime Marcelo Coello-Viejó, Silvia Carolina Zambonino-Torres
pmc-13111250.description: Gender equity remains a multidimensional and persistent challenge despite significant advances in public policy, health systems, labor structures, and sociocultural transformation. Existing research often approaches gender equity from fragmented perspectives, limiting a comprehensive understanding of its structural determinants and policy implications.

pmc-13440354.title: Facile, high‐throughput protein purification enabled by high‐efficiency protease elution
pmc-13440354.creator: Edson N Cárcamo Noriega, Ian S Truebridge, Frank D Teets, James W Bowman, Nathalia Rodriguez, Tessa A Howard, Christopher D Bahl
pmc-13440354.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While advances in artificial intelligence have made protein design widely accessible, protein production and characterization remain a bottleneck. Protease‐cleavable affinity tags are commonly used to improve yield and purity of recombinant proteins, but tag removal adds labor and complexity. Previous attempts to use a selective protease to elute cleaved fusion protein during affinity chromatography have suffered from poor digestion efficiency that greatly diminishes yield, or protease contamination in the eluate.
